source.title: Jacques Fuller: Sculptor
source.scope: Historical publication and exhibition catalogue; not a statement of current biography, studio location, ownership, or institutional affiliation.

paragraphs: After leaving school in Otjiwarongo in 1979, Jacques Fuller entered the police force in Namibia and completed National Service. He worked as a game ranger in Etosha in 1981-82, then settled in Bloemfontein in 1983 to work as an ornithological assistant at the National Museum.

He registered for a BA Fine Arts degree at the University of the Free State in 1984 and completed its practical component with distinction in sculpture in 1988. In 1989 he began working full-time as a sculptor from a smallholding at Bainsvlei outside Bloemfontein.

Jacques works directly in metal, using brass, steel, copper and found material. Rudimentary drawings are transferred to sheet metal as templates before each part is cut, shaped and assembled by hand. Figures, animals and mechanical forms carry humour, wordplay and social observation.

quotes.text: I would rather have someone look at my work twice, three times than have someone merely walk past without giving it a second glance.
quotes.speaker: Jacques Fuller

quotes.text: I prefer working directly with metal and having control of the entire process.
quotes.speaker: Jacques Fuller

quotes.text: I do make working drawings, which are rather rudimentary. I then transfer them directly onto the sheets of metal; in other words the drawing becomes a template.
quotes.speaker: Jacques Fuller

materialHistory.detail: Introduced to numerous sculptural techniques and materials, Jacques was drawn to working directly in metal.
Circular and square forms were layer-welded with gears and other found objects gathered from scrapyards.
A lighter, more pliable metal that introduced colour but required new solutions at welded joins.
A material Jacques described as combining the austerity of mild steel with the flexibility of red copper.
